countedIncomeFifthLimit1Dollars.citation: U.S. Census Bureau, Income in the United States: 2023 (P60-282), Table A-4, household income at the upper limit of the lowest fifth, 2023 dollars.
countedIncomeFifthLimit1Dollars.estimatedFrom: The upper limit of the lowest national household-income fifth keys a counted household's income band; the same limits apply in every place.

spread.citation: Within 5% of the published limit, covering the survey's margin and a year of price change.

countedIncomeFifthLimit2Dollars.citation: U.S. Census Bureau, Income in the United States: 2023 (P60-282), Table A-4, household income at the upper limit of the second fifth, 2023 dollars.
countedIncomeFifthLimit2Dollars.estimatedFrom: Upper limit of the second national household-income fifth.

countedIncomeFifthLimit3Dollars.citation: U.S. Census Bureau, Income in the United States: 2023 (P60-282), Table A-4, household income at the upper limit of the third fifth, 2023 dollars.
countedIncomeFifthLimit3Dollars.estimatedFrom: Upper limit of the third national household-income fifth.

countedIncomeFifthLimit4Dollars.citation: U.S. Census Bureau, Income in the United States: 2023 (P60-282), Table A-4, household income at the upper limit of the fourth fifth, 2023 dollars.
countedIncomeFifthLimit4Dollars.estimatedFrom: Upper limit of the fourth national household-income fifth.

countedWorkingAgeFrom.citation: BLS Current Population Survey: the civilian labor force age bands the opening's employment target uses (ACS/CPS 18 and over in the town's own employment receipt).
countedWorkingAgeFrom.estimatedFrom: Counted adults from this age without a recorded job share the place's unplaced workers.

countedWorkingAgeBelow.citation: Social Security Administration: full retirement age 66 to 67 for people born 1943 to 1960 and later; 65 is the age band edge the ACS employment tables and the opening's age bands use.
countedWorkingAgeBelow.estimatedFrom: Counted adults below this age without a recorded job share the place's unplaced workers.

countedOutlayShareOfDisposableIncome.citation: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, NIPA Table 2.1 'Personal Income and Its Disposition', 2019 annual: personal saving 7.3% of disposable personal income, so outlays are about 92.7% of income after taxes.
countedOutlayShareOfDisposableIncome.estimatedFrom: A counted group spends this share of its income after the taxes withheld from its pay (wages net, benefits and awards as paid), averaged over recent months; rent and mortgages come out of it first. 2019 avoids the pandemic years' saving.

spread.citation: BEA NIPA Table 2.1: saving 12% of disposable income in 2021 (the low end of outlays) to 3.5% in 2022 (the high end).

countedMovesInStateShare.citation: U.S. Census Bureau, CPS ASEC 2023, Geographical Mobility: 2022 to 2023, Table 1 (people 1 year and over): about 6.0 million moved from a different county in the same state and about 4.6 million from a different state, so 0.57 of those who left their county stayed in their state.
countedMovesInStateShare.estimatedFrom: Of a group's people who leave their county in a year (the ACS rate for their age), this share move elsewhere in their own state and the rest to another state or territory.

spread.citation: CPS ASEC 2019 to 2023 tables, same table each year.

countedMovesIncomeElasticity.citation: Kleven, Landais, Munoz and Stantcheva (2020), 'Taxation and Migration: Evidence and Policy Implications', Journal of Economic Perspectives 34(2): estimated elasticities of where people live to the after-tax income it offers run from near 0.1 for the whole population to about 1.8 for star scientists (Moretti and Wilson 2017) and above for some groups.
countedMovesIncomeElasticity.estimatedFrom: How strongly a place's pull follows its after-tax income in real terms (state income tax in force, regional prices) against home: the pull is scaled by that ratio to this power. A starting value inside the published range.

spread.unit: elasticity of the pull to the after-tax real income ratio
spread.citation: Kleven et al. (2020), Table 1 and section 3.

countedMovesUnemploymentPull.citation: Blanchard and Katz (1992), 'Regional Evolutions', Brookings Papers on Economic Activity: a state's relative unemployment drives net migration away from it within a few years; the size per point is a starting value.
countedMovesUnemploymentPull.estimatedFrom: Each point a place's unemployment runs below home multiplies its pull by exp(this); above home, the reverse.

spread.citation: Blanchard and Katz (1992); Dao, Furceri and Loungani (2017), Review of Economics and Statistics 99(2).

countedPeopleShareUnder18.citation: U.S. Census Bureau, Vintage 2024 national population estimates by age (NC-EST2024-AGESEX): about 21.5% of residents under 18.
countedPeopleShareUnder18.estimatedFrom: A state's or territory's people at the coarse grain, by age band, are its BEA population times the national shares.

spread.citation: State shares in the same estimates range about 19% to 25%.

countedPeopleShare18to29.citation: U.S. Census Bureau, Vintage 2024 national population estimates by age (NC-EST2024-AGESEX): about 16% of residents 18 to 29.
countedPeopleShare18to29.estimatedFrom: National share for the coarse grain.

spread.citation: State range in the same estimates.

countedPeopleShare30to44.citation: U.S. Census Bureau, Vintage 2024 national population estimates by age (NC-EST2024-AGESEX): about 19.9% of residents 30 to 44.
countedPeopleShare30to44.estimatedFrom: National share for the coarse grain.

spread.citation: State range in the same estimates.

countedPeopleShare45to64.citation: U.S. Census Bureau, Vintage 2024 national population estimates by age (NC-EST2024-AGESEX): about 24.6% of residents 45 to 64.
countedPeopleShare45to64.estimatedFrom: National share for the coarse grain.

spread.citation: State range in the same estimates.

countedPeopleShare65plus.citation: U.S. Census Bureau, Vintage 2024 national population estimates by age (NC-EST2024-AGESEX): about 18% of residents 65 and over.
countedPeopleShare65plus.estimatedFrom: National share for the coarse grain.

spread.citation: State range in the same estimates.

countedDemotionDays.citation: Owner, Oct 15, 2026: 'The days without contact before a met person drifts back into the counted population is a per-world range of 180 to 240 days, drawn once per world at generation (seeded generation is allowed), never a single fixed number.' Each world draws its own length in the spread from its seed; the value is the middle of the range.
countedDemotionDays.estimatedFrom: Days since the household was filled in and since the player's last contact with any of its people before it returns to the counts.

spread.citation: The owner's range (Oct 15, 2026); checked by the unit test in src/core2/counted-demotion.test.ts.

countedCommuterWorkdayHours.citation: BLS American Time Use Survey 2023: employed full-time people worked 8.4 hours on the days they worked (7.9 hours on average across all days worked by employed people); a commute job's workday is taken as 8 hours.
countedCommuterWorkdayHours.estimatedFrom: ATUS hours worked on days worked by full-time workers.

countedCommuterWorkdaysPerWeek.citation: A full-time work week is five days (BLS ATUS: employed people worked on 5.1 weekdays in an average week).
countedCommuterWorkdaysPerWeek.estimatedFrom: Weekday work shares in the ATUS.
